entry.title: Joining the Kostova lab at Stowers

link.title: Joining the Kostova lab at Stowers

entry.content:
In 2026, I joined Kamena Kostova’s lab at the Stowers Institute for Medical Research in Kansas City as an HHMI Gilliam Postdoctoral Research Fellow.

My current research focuses on ribosome quality control, including the quality control of defective large ribosomal subunit proteins in human cells.

This work builds on my interest in how cells recognize proteins for degradation, which I developed during my PhD in Olivia S. Rissland’s lab.

Read about my current research.
entry.summary: Beginning my postdoctoral work on ribosome quality control.

entry.title: PhD completed
entry.content:
I have officially earned my PhD in Molecular Biology & Biochemistry from the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus.

I began the program in 2018 and carried out my doctoral research with Olivia S. Rissland. My thesis project was Discovery and characterization of a MetAP-dependent N-degron pathway.

My PhD work examined how N-terminal sequence features and processing influence protein degradation. It also included work on N-terminal proteoform diversity and the characterization of 2A peptide-bond-skipping sequences.

Along the way, my training was supported by an NIH T32 fellowship, the NSF Graduate Research Fellowship, and the HHMI Gilliam Fellowship.

Explore my publications.

entry.title: Rising Stars in Biomedical Sciences
entry.content:
In May 2024, I was an invited speaker at SEP Rising Stars in Biomedical Sciences at Sanford Burnham Prebys in La Jolla, California.

My presentation, UBR4 regulates a MetAP2-dependent Arg/N-degron pathway, shared work from my PhD in Olivia S. Rissland’s lab at the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus.

Read the related preprint.
entry.summary: An invited research talk at Sanford Burnham Prebys.

entry.title: Research presentation award at SACNAS
entry.content:
In October 2023, I presented Tying up loose ends: Characterization of a novel N-degron pathway in humans at the SACNAS National Diversity in STEM Conference in Portland, Oregon.

The talk received an Outstanding Research Presentation award in Cell/Molecular Biology and Developmental Biology.

The presentation focused on my doctoral research in the Rissland lab at CU Anschutz. I also received a SACNAS NDiSTEM Travel Scholarship that year.

Read about the research behind the presentation.
entry.summary: Presenting my N-degron research at NDiSTEM 2023 in Portland.

entry.title: HHMI Gilliam Fellowship
entry.content:
My Howard Hughes Medical Institute Gilliam Fellowship began in September 2022, during my PhD in Molecular Biology & Biochemistry at the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus.

The supported project, A tripeptide motif induces rapid protein decay in human cells, investigated how short sequence features influence protein stability. I carried out this work in Olivia S. Rissland’s lab as part of my research on N-degron pathways.

Fellowship: HHMI Gilliam Fellowship, GT14919.

Explore the research.
entry.summary: A fellowship supporting my doctoral research on protein degradation.

entry.title: NSF Graduate Research Fellowship
entry.content:
My National Science Foundation Graduate Research Fellowship supported my doctoral research at the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus from June 2021 through August 2022.

The project, Primary protein sequence regulates gene expression, was part of my PhD work in Olivia S. Rissland’s lab. It sits within the question that shaped my doctoral research: how does the sequence at the beginning of a protein influence its fate?

Fellowship: NSF GRFP-2020300571.

More about my PhD research.
